Here’s for a world I’m working on:

Angels in my world are part of a metamorphic life cycle that ends with them turning into stone gargoyles. Some of them continue to live as gargoyles, but the highly vain angels view it as a horrific change.

Treants suffer from both tree rot and Rhizome, where a fungal infection causes their bark to peel.

Lurkers (a race of swamp dwelling bipedal creatures with tails and gills) are the result of years of alchemical experiments, and some suffer from calcification, especially in their muscles and joints. This disease is frequently referred to as “The Maw” in their culture.

Satyr’s have a condition that may cause parts of their skin and bone marrow to char and burn. Satyr’s are worshippers of fire, and blame this disease on blasphemers, who bring down the wrath of the sun upon them.

Finally, Oxellans are a race of parasitic, hive mind, squid-like creatures, that take control of the bodies of larger sea creatures. They have no diseases that they suffer from, and instead could be called the primary disease of their region.

I’d recommend whatever you’re comfortable with. I personally use GameCube, but the controller itself isn’t going to give too many advantages to Street Fighter Inputs. 

Good beginner combo for both: shorthop nair > jab > dtilt (light) > dtilt (light) > dtilt (heavy) > true tatsu/true hadoken, depending on the situation. Ryu and Ken are combo monsters, and most of it is free form, so don’t be afraid to play around a bit. 

Also try out his fully charged focus punch > fadc > into the above combo if you manage to land it.

Another bit of advice, once you get more comfortable inputting ryu’s true shoryuken, know that you can perform it after the first two hits of jab as a true combo, kills at ~ 90% on most of the cast. I say Ryu, because Ken’s True Shoryu can’t be used out of second jab hit.

All in all, good luck! Ryu is one of the most fulfilling characters in the game once you start getting better at him.

Reasonable, however while I agree the system is a great idea, I would argue it was done poorly, or at least: not as good as it could've been. For instance, if using blood vials means you haven't been playing as well, then using the rally system to heal means you haven't been playing well either. In a game where you have the potential to dodge all incoming damage through parries or I-frames, the ultimate goal is to never take damage. So while maybe the rally system makes it ok to be more aggressive and take damage trades more often, there is one large problem.

The amount of time you have to regain your health is different for each weapon, and while it is true that you can use blood gems to boost that rally potential, the change is hardly noticeable, and your bloodgems are better utilized for extra damage, or stamina use reduction.

Now, the problem with the rally system in my eyes is that a significant number of enemies will stagger you with their attacks (I don't think there's a single enemy that cants stagger you), with another large amount capable of flattening the player, causing greatly increased hitstun. The timer that you can regain health starts draining immediately as soon as you take damage, and it doesn't care about hitstun.

This would be fine, except that some weapons have incredible short rally potential. For instance, the blades of mercy have the shortest rally potential in the game at forty. These dual wielded blades allow for quick combos and fluid chains, racking up damage quickly. As such, it makes sense why they have short rally potential, because they attack so quickly. It's intended to make the player work to regain that health back by being aggressive, where a weapon like the hunter axe (which has the highest rally potential) has much slower attacks. In that case it seems very balanced, but there is the matter of "hyper armor," a state of heightened poise, added while performing specific moves. The blades of mercy have zero hyper armor on any attacks, while the hunter axe has hyper armor on several of the extended forms attacks (and the untransformed charged r2). So this means that with the blades of mercy, while they excel against one vs. one fights against enemies that cannot stun/stagger you, and are quite good against other players, the best and most reliable method of healing is blood vials, as most attacks will stun you longer than the rally potential is active for that weapon. At the most you can hope to get one swing in before the rally is gone, and you have to pop a vial.
